subject: Preserve multiplicity for friend-appended BattleDecisions targets
description: SuN1Sh1nE Profile_004 Savegame_002 replay-009 advanced past task 138 and diverged after frame 36627 because Soldier 194's Rust mlistThem was [PC343, PC345] while Original retained [PC343]. The visible divergence occurred when Soldier 194's BowObserving timer rebuilt its personal Them list to [PC343], then BattleDecisions imported nearby attacking Soldier 193's primary target. The hidden choice had already diverged five frames earlier: at frame 36622 Soldier 193 personally saw only PC343, then its friend scan appended PC345 from Soldier 194 before ArcherObserve selected a target. Original stores primary-target multiplicity on each human and resets it only for enemies already present in mlistThem at BattleDecisions entry. PC343 was therefore reset to zero, while newly appended PC345 retained its live shared multiplicity from Soldier 194's existing claim. Rust modeled the decision with a local map initialized only from the entry Them list but incorrectly treated every absent, later-appended target as zero, making PC345 appear unoccupied and selecting it. That hidden PC345 selection became observable at frame 36627 when Soldier 194 imported Soldier 193's target. Friend-appended targets now seed their count from the owner-boundary shared primary_target_multiplicity snapshot before any source-authored swordfight increment, while entry Them targets retain their explicit zero reset. This composes with task 134's source-faithful stacking and live-primary-target work. Focused coverage verifies that an entry target stays reset despite a nonzero shared count, a newly appended target retains its shared count, and a subsequent friend increment stacks on that retained value. cargo test -p robin_engine appended_battle_target_retains_global_multiplicity_after_personal_reset passes 1/1, cargo fmt is clean, and git diff --check is clean.
